title_en: The Oneness of God in Worship
body_ar:
لقد أرسل الله الرسل يدعون إلى إفراد الله بالعبادة، وينهون عما يخل بذلك أو يؤدي إلى نقيضه من الشرك كتعبيد الأسماء لغير الله، والتبرك الممنوع، كما نهوا عن التمسح بالقبور والنذر لغير الله أو الذبح للأموات وغير ذلك.
وجوب إفراد الله بالعبادة:
قال: [فأفردوه جل بالعباده لا تشركوا في نوعها عباده] الفاء هنا للترتيب على ما سبق، ومعناه: إذا اجتنبتم الشرك فأفردوا الله، أي: وحدوه بالعبادة، وهذا هو الذي يسميه أهل السلوك بالتخلي قبل التحلي. فالتخلي يقتضي التخلص من الشرك. والتحلي يقتضي التحلي والاتصاف بالتوحيد. فيجمع الإنسان بين النفي والإثبات فينفي الشرك أولاً ثم يثبت التوحيد ثانياً، وهذان الأمران تضمنتهما كلمة التوحيد: لا إله إلا الله، فـ(لا إله) نفي، و(إلا الله) إثبات، فلذلك بدأ أولاً بنفي الشرك ثم رتب عليه إثبات التوحيد في قوله: (فأفردوه جل بالعبادة)...
body_en:
*[Site synopsis]* God sent the messengers calling to the devoting of worship to God alone, and forbidding whatever impairs that or leads to its opposite in the way of associating partners with God (shirk) — such as making names into names of servitude to other than God, and the forbidden seeking of blessing. They likewise forbade rubbing oneself against graves, making vows to other than God, and slaughtering for the dead, and other things of that kind.

## The obligation to devote worship to God alone

He said: *[So devote worship to Him alone, exalted is He; do not associate His servants with Him in any kind of it.]* The "so" here is a connective ordering this upon what preceded, and the meaning is: once you have avoided associating partners with God, devote worship to God alone — that is, single Him out for worship. This is what the people of the spiritual path call divesting before adorning. Divesting requires ridding oneself of associating partners with God; adorning requires taking on and being characterised by the affirmation of God's oneness. So a person joins negation and affirmation together: he negates association first, and then affirms God's oneness second. These two things are what the word of oneness, "there is no god but God", contains: "there is no god" is negation, and "but God" is affirmation. For this reason he began first with the negation of association, and then ordered upon it the affirmation of oneness, in his words: *(So devote worship to Him alone, exalted is He.)* …

flags.context: the record breaks off and the full text sits behind a download
options: render with an excerpt banner and link the .doc
flags.note: Excerpt only, style guide section 9. It breaks off on an ellipsis at the end of the commentary on the first hemistich, so that the second hemistich — the prohibition of associating God's servants with Him — is quoted but not expounded, and none of the specific practices listed in the synopsis is discussed. The complete text sits behind /medias/doc/L-33.doc. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends and completes nothing. Must not be rendered as a whole lesson.

flags.arabic: الفقرة الافتتاحية مقابل ما بعد العنوان الفرعي
flags.context: the synopsis paragraph against the transcribed opening of the lesson
options: mark the synopsis as the site's own and the remainder as the Sheikh's words
present the whole record as the Sheikh's words
flags.note: The record has two authors. The first paragraph is a synopsis written by the site — it speaks about the lesson and its subject in the third person and does not begin with the opening formula. Everything from the section heading onward is transcribed speech in the Sheikh's own voice. The site must not present the synopsis as his words.

flags.context: the formula introducing each quoted line of the versified creed being commented on
options: read it as the author of the versified base text, distinct from the lecturer
read it as Sheikh al-Dedew quoting his own verse
flags.note: Getting this referent wrong would misattribute a creedal formulation, so it is flagged on every record in which the formula appears. These lessons are a commentary on a versified creed (nazm): the transcriber introduces each base-text line with 'the Sheikh, may God preserve him, said', and the commentary follows. 'حفظه الله' is used of the living, which at first sight fits Sheikh al-Dedew himself. Three passages inside the run settle it otherwise. Record 719 has the speaker giving thanks for 'completing the commentary on the Sheikh's versification' and describing what 'the Sheikh' chose to leave undetailed — a commentator does not ordinarily speak of his own base text that way while expounding it. Record 716 describes the base text as a versification of the Mukhtaṣar of Khalil ibn Ishaq by 'one of the scholars'. Record 718 introduces the same quoted lines with 'the versifier said'. The reading adopted throughout this slice is therefore that 'the Sheikh' is the living author of the versified base text and the lecturer is his commentator. The author is nowhere named, and the identification should be confirmed by the Sheikh's office before publication, because the bracketed verse and the prose around it carry different attributions.

flags.context: the gloss on the pair التخلي / التحلي
options: preserve the doubled word in body_ar and translate the evident sense
read a transcription doubling and drop the repeated word in body_ar
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT, style guide section 11. The sentence defines 'التحلي' by repeating 'التحلي' — the term defined stands inside its own definition, while the parallel sentence about 'التخلي' immediately before it is well formed. Almost certainly a transcription doubling. The Arabic is preserved exactly; the English renders the evident sense, 'taking on and being characterised by', without repairing the Arabic.

flags.context: the Sheikh's attribution of the phrase to أهل السلوك
flags.note: A fixed pair from the vocabulary of spiritual wayfaring, built on a rhyme the English cannot keep. 'Divesting' and 'adorning' were chosen because 'تحلي' is specifically to put on ornament, which 'filling' loses. The Sheikh attributes the phrase to 'أهل السلوك' and the English keeps the attribution visible: he is reporting their term, not coining it.

flags.arabic: كتعبيد الأسماء لغير الله، والتبرك الممنوع
flags.context: the practices listed in the site's synopsis
options: making names into names of servitude to other than God, and the forbidden seeking of blessing
naming people as servants of other than God, and impermissible seeking of blessing
flags.note: A list of specific practices declared to impair the devotion of worship to God alone, including rubbing oneself against graves, vows to other than God and slaughtering for the dead. These are contested between Muslim currents and an English page listing them will be read partisanly; style guide section 12 applies. Two points for the reviewer. The list is the site's synopsis, not the Sheikh's transcribed words — the lesson as served never reaches any of these practices. And 'التبرك الممنوع' is itself qualified: the synopsis forbids a specified kind of seeking blessing, not the practice as such, and the English keeps the qualifier attached.

options: The obligation to devote worship to God alone
The necessity of worshipping God alone
flags.note: 'وجوب' here attaches to an act — devoting worship — and so is the legal ruling, rendered 'obligation' per the fixed mapping. It is not the kalām modality of record 711 and must not be read as such. The heading is the site's, and the transcribed portion states the obligation only by expounding an imperative in the base verse.

translator_notes: One of a run of fifteen records, IDs 707-721, in the written-creed section, all uploaded on 9 and 10 May 2011 within a few hours of one another, all built to the same template and all excerpts. Each carries a site-written synopsis, then a section heading, then the opening formula and the first lines of a lesson, and then breaks off on an ellipsis; the full text sits behind a .doc download in the /medias/doc/L-* series, numbered L-26 to L-39 in the same order as the IDs. The uniform timestamps are a bulk upload and say nothing about when the lesson was delivered.

The record contains two distinct voices and the English keeps them apart. The opening paragraph is a synopsis written by the site, about the lesson and in the third person; everything from the section heading onward is the Sheikh's own words as transcribed. Nothing in the synopsis may be quoted as his.

The source's final line, 'تحميل المادة' ('download the material'), is the label of a download link in the page furniture, not part of the text. It is recorded as source_download_link and omitted from body_ar and body_en.

The base text being commented on is identified inside this run. Record 719 has the Sheikh speaking of 'completing the commentary on the Sheikh's versification', and of that versifier's rendering of Khalil's Jāmiʿ in some five hundred lines; record 716 describes the base text as a versification of the Mukhtaṣar of Khalil ibn Ishaq whose opening section is on creed; and record 718 introduces the same quoted lines with 'the versifier said'. Taken together these settle that 'the Sheikh, may God preserve him' in this run is the living author of the versified base text and not the lecturer. The author is never named.
This record's transcribed portion opens with a bare 'قال' where the others in the run have 'قال الشيخ حفظه الله'. The English gives 'He said' and supplies no subject.
The verse is given without diacritics and without the hamzah on 'العبادة' and 'عباده'; these are the source's orthography and are preserved in body_ar.
'أهل السلوك' is rendered 'the people of the spiritual path' rather than 'the Sufis', which the Arabic does not say.
